tagline: Historic town streets and a two-car crossing of the Meherrin River
intro: Lafayette’s Tour appears among North Carolina’s Coastal Plain scenic byways. The North Carolina Department of Transportation selects these routes to introduce the state’s history, geography and culture. The places here range from Warrenton’s preserved nineteenth-century houses to Halifax on the Roanoke River and the cable ferry over the Meherrin. Halifax stands near the Fall Line, where North Carolina’s Piedmont meets its Coastal Plain.

River access helped Halifax develop near the Roanoke’s head of navigation. Farther east, Murfreesboro’s 1787 charter provided for a public dock at the northernmost point of navigation on the Meherrin.

Begin with Warrenton’s historic streets and Halifax’s riverside setting. Murfreesboro occupies high ground south of the Meherrin. Parker’s Ferry crosses that river near its meeting with the Chowan; farther east, Sunbury stands at US 158 and NC 32.

moments.title: Warrenton
moments.text: Warrenton’s historic streets began with a hundred half-acre lots. William Christmas surveyed and laid out the streets, lots and public squares in 1779. The town became a regional trading center for tobacco and cotton plantations. Its building trade reached beyond town: Jacob Holt built Greek Revival houses across the region, and his workshop supplied millwork farther afield. Many early- and mid-nineteenth-century houses survive, while commercial and government buildings date to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The historic district includes more than two hundred contributing buildings and entered the National Register in 1976.

moments.title: Halifax
moments.text: Halifax developed near the Roanoke River’s head of navigation, close to the Fall Line between the Piedmont and Coastal Plain. By the American Revolution it had become a commercial and political center. Established in 1757, the town became the new county’s seat two years later. North Carolina’s Fourth Provincial Congress met here in spring 1776 and adopted the Halifax Resolves on April 12. The historic district is operated as a historic site by the North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources. The William R. Davie House, Eagle Tavern and Sally-Billy House are among the town’s National Register properties.

moments.title: Parker's Ferry
moments.text: Parker’s Ferry is a steel barge with room for two cars, guided across the Meherrin by a cable. A diesel engine and propeller supply the power. The cable normally lies underwater; rollers lift it as the vessel crosses and keep the ferry on course in normal currents. The crossing connects Maney’s Neck with southern Hertford County. Steel posts secure the cable on each bank, while the operator controls the engine from a room at the side of the barge. Drivers on the opposite bank summon the ferry with their horn.

practical: Parker's Ferry: The ferry carries at most two cars and does not operate during high water or storms. (checked 2026-10-11)
